title: CRAH units — sequence of operations
note: PRD-SETPOINT-SIM P3. Curated; thresholds resolved by tools/build-sequences.mjs (see chiller.json).

basis.ref: ASHRAE Guideline 36-2021, computer-room air handler sequences
basis.use: the structure: the CHW valve holds the supply air setpoint, fans follow the load, standby start on a unit failure
basis.limits: the numbers come from this plant's engine, limits registry and control registry, not from the guideline

plant: per hall: the fewest CRAHs that carry the hall load plus one standby (N+1, js/conv-engine.js crah_installed = crah_required + 1); a unit's rating is its sensible capacity

modes.label: Normal — supply air control

entry.text: hall cooling enabled and the duty CRAHs proven (airflow proven, no fault)

actions: each CRAH's CHW valve holds its supply air at the setpoint
fan speed follows the hall load (the engine's fan speed = unit duty share of the rating)
rotate the standby unit by run hours

exit.event: a running CRAH fails (fan, airflow or controller fault)

exit.text: supply air above its setpoint with the CHW valve fully open

assumed.delay_s 300: 5 min confirmation before acting on a high air temperature; no source in this repo states it

modes.label: CRAH failure — standby start
actions: lock out the failed unit and raise an alarm
start the standby CRAH at once
the remaining fans run to full speed; rack inlet rises while sensible capacity is short

exit.event: the standby CRAH is proven running

modes.label: High rack inlet — all units
actions: every fan to full speed, every CHW valve fully open
alarm to the operator; check the CHW supply (chiller plant sequence)
